newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia bond yields end higher,shorts outperform.
newsitem.headline: Australia bond yields end higher,shorts outperform.

text.p: *Australian bond yields ended a thinly traded session higher in the wake of Friday's sell-off in U.S. Treasuries, although the short end gave up only a little ground.

Australian bond yields ended a thinly traded session higher in the wake of Friday's sell-off in U.S. Treasuries, although the short end gave up only a little ground causing the yield curve to steepen.

"It was a pretty good performance by the short end in the current environment," said one trader. "The long end is awaiting the next big figure from the U.S., but at current levels it is showing a more measured approach to the U.S. than say a month ago when yields were at 7.75 percent."
The U.S., which came under pressure on Friday on its PPI and retails sales data, faces the March CPI on Tuesday.
The domestic short end remained underpinned by last week's weak labour force report, which has encouraged talk that the Reserve Bank may ease policy again.

However, the market will need to see the Australian CPI next week, average weekly earnings data next month and the outcome to the "living wage" claim, which still remains in limbo, before pricing in such a move, analysts said.
Expectations of a benign inflation outcome has already seen the long end outperform the U.S. since the beginning of the month to see the spread squeeze in to just over 100 basis points.

"In the near term, the spread may fluctuate between 100-120 basis points with the potential to go through 100 basis points on the back of forthcoming bond friendly data," said Su-Lin Ong, fixed income economist at Hambros Bank.
However, she saw the spread widening out to 150 basis points in the next six months as economic data pointed to a stronger economy and possible inflationary concerns.

Today's manufacturing output prices for February showed only a modest 0.2 percent rise, while housing finance for the same month fell 6.9 percent and coming within a wide range of expectations. There was no market reaction to either report.
By 5.30 p.m., and in early after hours trading, the local long end had reversed its initial spread widening against the U.S., while shorts made further inroads on the differential.
However, the market dragged its heels against New Zealand debt, which is expecting a benign outcome to Tuesday's N.Z. CPI.
